bodyHTML:
Contributing guidelines

  • I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)

mini.surround

Question

mini.surround supports 'tags', which works great also for JSX (including the <></> empty tag which is a thing in JSX).

However it seems TSX generic components are not recognized as 'tags'. For instance, see:
https://mariusschulz.com/blog/passing-generics-to-jsx-elements-in-typescript

If I just modify a little that example...

function Form() {
  // ...

  return (
    <Select<string>
      options={targets}
      value={target}
      onChange={setTarget}
    >
     <Item key="1" />
     <Item key="2" />
    </Select>
  );
}

Now if I put the cursor before the <Item key="1" />, on that line, and type srt, i would like for surround to realize I'm talking about the Select tag. Ideally it would then allow me to replace the whole Select<string> of the start tag, and the Select of the end tag. Same for sdt and so on.

I do realize it's a bizarre syntax and really a torture test... But it's a real use-case so I thought I'd ask.

I imagine this could be sorted out using custom surroundings, and maybe using treesitter, or a regex. I tried a little, but didn't make it quickly. If noone answers and I manage to make it work, i'll paste my solution here, but i'll be grateful if someone beats me to it :)

comment_data.body:
I am afraid, this is a too complicated use case for built-in `t` because it uses Lua patterns. Account for a `Select<string>` as a tag name is very not trivial with the Lua pattern surrounding specification (because it needs to "know" that `>` after `string` does not close the tag).

As always the case with tag surrounding and textobject, the suggestion is to use tree-sitter to define them. This might or might not require writing custom tree-sitter queries, which is not trivial.

> Now if I put the cursor before the `<Item key="1" />`, on that line, and type `srt`, i would like for surround to realize I'm talking about the `Select` tag. Ideally it would then allow me to replace the whole `Select<string>` of the start tag, and the `Select` of the end tag. Same for `sdt` and so on.

I am pretty sure that `sdt` deleting only `Select<string>` in opening tag and `Select` in closing tag is expected. This will lead to something like `<options={targets} ... > ... </>` which is probably not what is usually the goal. The `sdt` arguably needs to delete the whole left+right tag pair and preserve only inside the tag.

As both "delete" and first step of "replace" share the logic of finding the target region, it is not possible to achieve this with a single surrounding. There has to be separate `tag` and `tag_name` surrounding. For example:
- Reference text `<tag kind="val">Text</tag>`
- The `tag` surrounding would match `<tag kind="val">` on left and `</tag>` on right.
- The `tag_name` surrounding would match `tag` on left and `tag` on right.

---

Here is my attempt on enabling this kind of behavior for tsx files using tree-sitter (make sure to use 'nvim-treesitter' on `main` branch):

- Create a file '~/.config/nvim/after/queries/tsx/textobjects.scm' with the following content (**Edit**: [this comment](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2079#discussioncomment-14742926) contains better queries):

    ```scm
    ; extends

    (jsx_element
      open_tag: (_)
      (_)+ @tag.inner ; Capture everything between open and close tag
                      ; This works because 'mini.surround' computes matching
                      ; region based on all captures: from the start of the leftmost
                      ; one to the end of the rightmost one (i.e. union of regions).
      close_tag: (_)) @tag.outer

    ; For @tag_name.inner + @tag_name.outer pair to work with 'mini.surround', they
    ; need to capture so that the different between them is left and right tag name.
    ; So something like this:
    ; - `@tag_name.inner` should capture everything to the right of left tag name
    ;   up until the start of the right tag name (including `</`).
    ;   In the query this is done by making multiple captures, which works because
    ;   'mini.surround' matches a region based on their union.
    ; - `@tag_name.outer` should capture `@tag_name.inner` PLUS left and right names.
    (
     (jsx_element
        open_tag: (jsx_opening_element
          name: (identifier) @tag_name.outer ; Match the tag name (e.g., Select), but DO NOT capture it
          (_)* @tag_name.inner; Match and capture everything else after tag name
        )
        (_)+ @tag_name.inner ; Match everything inside
        close_tag: ( jsx_closing_element
          (_)* @tag_name.inner; Match and capture everything before tag name
          name: (identifier) @tag_name.outer
        )
      )
      (#offset! @tag_name.inner 0 0 0 2) ; Extend inner capture by 2 to the right
                                         ; to also match `</`
    )
    ```

- Use the following 'mini.surround' setup:

    ```lua
    local ts_input = require('mini.surround').gen_spec.input.treesitter
    require('mini.surround').setup({
      custom_surroundings = {
        -- Use tree-sitter to search for function call
        t = {
          input = ts_input({ outer = '@tag.outer', inner = '@tag.inner' }),
        },
        T = {
          input = ts_input({ outer = '@tag_name.outer', inner = '@tag_name.inner' }),
          output = function()
            local tag_name = MiniSurround.user_input('Tag name')
            return { left = tag_name, right = tag_name }
          end,
        },
      },
    })
    ```

Now `sdt` will delete/find/highlight the whole `tag` correctly.

The `srTT` works in limited cases, but my tree-sitter querying knowledge is limited here, I am afraid.

Let's hope there will be an improvement in this area with time.

What versions do you mean here? If queries, then they should already be separated by putting them in a specially named files (`queries/tsx/textobjects.scm` and `queries/<other-lang>/textobjects.scm`).

If you want to adjust surroundings based on the language, then you can use [buffer-local configs](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-surround.html#module-setup). Here is an [example from MiniMax](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/515c6ea7361ab11d8f6024e35b4068b06e528aed/configs/nvim-0.11/after/ftplugin/markdown.lua#L27-L42).

comment_data.body:
A query for `tag_name` that doesn't require the `offset` directive is

```query
(jsx_element
  open_tag: (jsx_opening_element
    name: (identifier) @tag_name.outer
    (_)* @tag_name.inner
    ">" @tag_name.inner)
  _+ @tag_name.inner
  close_tag: (jsx_closing_element
    "</" @tag_name.inner
    (_)* @tag_name.inner
    name: (identifier) @tag_name.outer))
```

I also played with queries for a self closing tag

```query
(jsx_self_closing_element) @tag.outer

(jsx_self_closing_element
  (jsx_attribute)+ @tag.inner)
```

and

```query

(jsx_self_closing_element
  name: (_) @tag_name.outer
  (_)* @tag_name.outer @tag_name.inner)
```

But, in both cases, for `tag_name` the difference between the `inner` and `outer` regions do not include possible trailing whitespace after the tag name, which may result in a malformed tag name unless a space is inserted. (There's also the need to special case the `output` of the self closing tag to return `""` as the right side of the surrounding).
